question.text: A galvanometer of resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> is connected to a battery of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> along with a resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3000</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>. In this case, a full-scale deflection of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>units</mi></math> is obtained in the galvanometer. In order to reduce this deflection to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>units</mi></math>, how much more resistance (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>) should be added to the circuit in series?

solution.text:
The deflection in a galvanometer is directly proportional to the current.

First case:

30x=225+3000

Second case:

10x=225+3000+R

⇒3=25+3000+R25+3000

On solving, we get

R=6050 Ω
